extracted.intended_audience: teachers and students using a classroom rubric to evaluate or submit creative-writing short stories
extracted.subtask_description: A classroom-oriented rubric for evaluating student short stories, covering presentation, creativity, character and plot development, grammar, and conflict. Designed for instructors to score stories out of 100 across six categories with four performance levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Presentation (15 pts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates the structural completeness and adherence to formatting and submission directions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: Needs Improvement — Structurally inferior; did not follow directions. Fair — Typed but with incorrect font/size; missing name, date, class. Good — Typed with possibly missing or misspelled header information. Excellent — Times New Roman 12 font; name, date, class present. (Worth 15 points total.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Creativity & Use of Literary Devices (10 pts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses originality, use of creative/descriptive language, and incorporation of literary devices that engage readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: Needs Improvement — No creative language; lacks feeling and emotion. Fair — Few creative terms; may be out of context. Good — Some creative language; devices present but disrupt story flow. Excellent — "Story is filled with creative and descriptive language" engaging readers. (Worth 10 points total.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Character Development (15 pts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Measures how well characters are developed, including descriptive detail and depth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: Needs Improvement — Lacks descriptive details; characters lack depth. Fair — Reader gains basic character understanding. Good — Some descriptive details; characters somewhat interesting. Excellent — Thorough development through speech, actions, description. (Worth 15 points total.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Plot Development (30 pts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges the story's structural development and completeness of narrative sequence and key plot components.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: Needs Improvement — No development; lacks sequence. Fair — Needs improvement; missing pieces. Good — Follows sequence but components need better development. Excellent — Contains exposition, rising action, climax, falling action, resolution. (Worth 30 points total.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Grammar (15 pts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluates mechanical correctness (grammar, punctuation, spelling) as it affects readability and storytelling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels keyed to number of errors: Needs Improvement — 9+ errors interfering with storytelling. Fair — 7–9 errors. Good — 3–6 errors. Excellent — 1–2 grammatical errors. (Worth 15 points total.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Conflict (15 pts)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assesses clarity and development of the central conflict and how well the story is developed around it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Levels: Needs Improvement — No conflict presented. Fair — Vague or unclear conflict. Good — Conflict depicted; story somewhat developed around it. Excellent — "Conflict is clearly depicted in the story and the story is developed around the conflict." (Worth 15 points total.)
